description.short_caption: Erythematous papules and pustules on the lower legs.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the lower legs of a patient with multiple erythematous papules and pustules scattered across the skin. The lesions vary in size and are distributed irregularly. Some lesions appear to have central crusting or ulceration, suggesting possible secondary infection or necrosis. The surrounding skin appears otherwise unremarkable.
visible_findings: central crusting or ulceration in some lesions

description.short_caption: Skin lesion with central ulceration and surrounding erythema.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a single skin lesion with a central ulceration surrounded by a ring of erythema. The lesion appears circular with a slightly raised border and a central darkened area. The surrounding skin shows mild erythema and is covered with fine hair. The lesion is consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process.

Case_11003/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Hematoxylin and eosin stain of skin biopsy.

description.short_caption: Hematoxylin and eosin stain of skin biopsy showing superficial and deep perivascular lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate.
description.detailed_description: This image shows two sections of skin biopsy stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The epidermis is intact, with a slightly thickened appearance. The dermis demonstrates a prominent superficial and deep perivascular lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, as indicated by the labeled arrows. The infiltrate is dense and localized around blood vessels, consistent with an inflammatory process. The stain highlights cellular and structural details, aiding in the assessment of the tissue pathology.
visible_findings: superficial and deep perivascular lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate
dense inflammatory infiltrate around blood vessels

description.detailed_description: This image shows a tissue biopsy stained with an immunohistochemical (IHC) stain targeting Treponema pallidum. The spirochetes are visible as thin, spiral-shaped organisms highlighted in brown against a blue background of cellular structures. The staining technique enhances the visibility of the organisms within the tissue, confirming their presence.

description.short_caption: Hematoxylin and eosin stain of skin biopsy showing inflammatory infiltrate and fungal elements.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained section of skin tissue. The dermis contains a dense inflammatory infiltrate composed of lymphocytes and histiocytes. Two circled areas highlight fungal elements, appearing as round to oval structures with clear halos, consistent with yeast forms. The epidermis appears intact, and no significant necrosis is visible.
visible_findings: dense inflammatory infiltrate in the dermis
circled fungal elements resembling yeast forms
